records.title: Al Boraq: the original corridor and its changing network
aliases: Ligne à grande vitesse Tanger Kénitra
records.answer: Al Boraq combines a purpose-built high-speed railway north of Kénitra with through running over conventional tracks towards Rabat and Casablanca. Understanding that interface explains why new trains, later extensions and everyday service need separate evidence.
records.scope: The initial Tangier–Kénitra high-speed railway and its Al Boraq through-service interface to Rabat and Casablanca, counted as one project. Excludes the later Kénitra–Marrakech extension and its fleet order. Stations and trainsets are components, not additional identities.
records.stage: November 2018 inauguration and subsequent passenger operation documented. Later expansion orders and construction plans remain separate from accepted capacity and recurring reliability.

identity_decision.rationale: The funder distinguishes the new Tangier–Kénitra line from its connection to the conventional railway. Al Boraq is the service name, not another project. The original corridor counts once; the later Marrakech extension, its train order and individual stations do not add delivery within this identity. No historical acquisition docket is reused.

timeline.event: Supplier dates the inauguration; this is not assigned as the exact commercial-service start.
Supplier announces the eighteen-train Horizon order for later expansion.
Government page publishes an operating-service retrospective and future capacity plans; its MAP dispatch is April 24.
ONCF's announced Casablanca works and staged service arrangements are relayed by the government portal.

sections.heading: One service across two kinds of railway
sections.text: Al Boraq’s original infrastructure is the new line from Tangier to Kénitra, where trains join the conventional network towards Rabat and Casablanca. AFD’s project account distinguishes those two parts and reports 5.6 million Al Boraq passengers in 2025. Its whole-network figure belongs to a different denominator. This is a useful account of corridor use, not a measure of punctuality or avoided road journeys. The funder’s long-running project record also describes financing and development: its status cannot be read as saying that the railway has never opened. Through running, rather than a second counted project, connects the two infrastructure types.

sections.heading: Vehicles and signalling at the interface
sections.text: Alstom’s November 15, 2018 inauguration account describes twelve double-deck Euroduplex trainsets with equipment for both high-speed and conventional operation. It identifies ERTMS signalling compatibility and accommodation for passengers with reduced mobility, alongside Arabic and French information. These features explain how a single train can serve a mixed corridor without passengers changing at its infrastructure boundary. They describe supplied equipment, not a recurring record of accessible journeys. The inauguration date should also remain distinct from an exact public commercial-service start. Supplier capability claims are useful technical context, but sustained reliability depends on the operation and maintenance that follow delivery.

sections.heading: Capacity planning beyond a faster journey
sections.text: The government’s April 2025 retrospective presents Al Boraq as an operating intercity service and places its future development within a wider network strategy. Moving more fast trains onto new infrastructure is intended to release existing tracks for other services, including metropolitan transport. That is a capacity-allocation proposition: the benefit depends on the subsequent timetable, train availability and local service offer, not simply the existence of another line. It also links national railway investment to the cities receiving the trains. Promotional economic and environmental claims in this account are not treated as measured effects on particular neighbourhoods or passengers.

sections.heading: An expansion order is a different delivery stage
sections.text: The March 28, 2025 supplier announcement records an order for eighteen Avelia Horizon trains, financed by the French Treasury at a stated €781 million. It connects those trains with future service towards Marrakech. This is later expansion, outside the original counted corridor, rather than an increase already available to its passengers. The new platform’s proposed operating and maintenance advantages likewise belong to the supplier’s expectations. A delivery account would need to identify the trainsets received, testing completed and service introduction. Keeping those steps separate allows the reader to follow genuine progress without treating procurement as operational acceptance.

sections.heading: Expansion work also affects the railway already in use
sections.text: ONCF’s September 2, 2025 statement describes works around Casablanca, especially between Mohammedia and Nouaceur, with additional tracks intended to separate fast, local and other services. It announces staged works from September 2025 through the end of 2027 and warns of timetable changes and temporary station closures. The proposed first phase starts September 15, after passenger-assistance arrangements from September 8. These dates define an announced construction and service-management sequence, not observed continuity or completed works. For the original corridor, the practical dependency is clear: through passengers use a receiving network that can be disrupted while it is expanded.

sections.heading: Editorial test for a dependable end-to-end service
sections.text: Follow a defined set of journeys from origin station to final urban destination. Record the service offered, cancellations, actual arrival times and the usability of station access over comparable periods. Keep construction-related changes visible, and distinguish infrastructure capability from the timetable passengers receive. Ridership can show use without explaining who benefits or which trips were replaced. New fleet evidence should identify accepted units and their service dates before it changes an operating-capacity claim. This approach would connect the national corridor with Tangier and Casablanca’s local systems while preserving separate responsibilities, project boundaries and meaningful measures of everyday access.

next_artifacts: Comparable Al Boraq service and accessibility results with stable journey and period definitions.
Dated accepted-fleet and service-introduction records for later orders, outside the original project's delivery count.
Actual construction-period service and station-access records, distinct from advance timetable plans.

records.title: Tangier: municipal access beyond the high-speed station
records.answer: Tangier’s city account connects municipal responsibilities with the coach terminal, parking access and the care of local green space. The intercity railway is one connection within that everyday service system, not a substitute for it.
records.scope: Commune de Tanger, counted as one place across Tanger-Médina, Bni Makada, Souani and Mghogha. Excludes Tangier-Assilah prefecture, the Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceïma region and the wider Tanger Med port system. Arrondissements are components of the commune.
records.stage: Historical municipal identity and dated terminal, parking and public-space accounts inspected. Announced rules and works are not current compliance or city-wide outcome acceptance.

identity_decision.rationale: The municipal identity page names one commune and its four arrondissements. Its prefecture-level population does not enlarge the city boundary or provide a commune denominator. Tangier-Assilah, the wider region and the port system remain related but distinct geographies. No historical acquisition docket is reused.

timeline.event: Municipal historical page places the unified-city commune's establishment in this year, without an exact day.
Coach-terminal account retrospectively dates the opening at Hararine.
Municipality publishes terminal use through December 26, not a full-year total.
Municipality reports the start of Rahrah-site works with a six-month expectation.
Parking notice announces a July 9 start for the delegated paid-parking areas.
Announced effective date for the parking provisions, not an observed compliance finding.

sections.heading: The commune is not the surrounding prefecture
sections.text: Tangier’s historical municipal page describes a unified city established in 2002 and identifies four arrondissements: Tanger-Médina, Bni Makada, Souani and Mghogha. This account uses that commune as its place boundary. The population cited on the same page refers to Tangier-Assilah prefecture and should not become the denominator for municipal coverage. The distinction also prevents the wider region and Tanger Med port system from being folded into one synthetic city result. Districts remain parts of the same counted place. The page is labelled old, so its historical identity is useful without turning its officeholder details into a current governance roster.

sections.heading: Local responsibilities connect movement and maintenance
sections.text: The municipality’s explanation of its functions groups responsibilities into its own, shared and transferred competences. It places transport, traffic and parking alongside lighting, sanitation, waste and public spaces, while describing a six-year action programme with nearer-term resource estimates. This is a practical reminder that access involves more than a transport line: a destination also depends on the street and services around it. The explanation is not a performance audit or inspection of the underlying legal instrument. It provides a framework for locating responsibility, then asking which budget, contract and service record demonstrates delivery in a particular neighbourhood.

sections.heading: A coach terminal moves journeys towards the edge
sections.text: The municipality dates the Hararine coach terminal’s opening to November 1, 2019 and describes its location near Ring Road 9 and provincial road 4605. Moving the terminal from the centre was intended to ease central bus congestion. The December 2022 account reports 1,277,730 travellers from January 1 through December 26, not the entire calendar year. That count describes use of the terminal rather than a measured congestion reduction. For passengers, an outer terminal also makes the connecting urban leg important. Its location and patronage therefore raise a separate access question about reaching the terminal, not just boarding an intercity coach.

sections.heading: Parking reform has a defined service area
sections.text: The July 4, 2025 notice announces implementation from July 9 within paid-parking areas under delegated management. It describes ending wheel clamping, free parking for people with disabilities, dedicated spaces and preferential subscriptions for residents and traders. These are distinct changes to enforcement, accessibility and local access, not a city-wide claim that every parking space follows the same arrangements. The notice establishes an announced rule and rollout date, rather than observed compliance or a current tariff. Its practical value depends on understandable signs, usable reserved spaces and consistent treatment of the people covered by the provisions.

sections.heading: Rahrah links public space with ecological care
sections.text: The June 12, 2023 municipal account reports work beginning around Lake Rahrah, with municipal technical studies and designs. It describes green-space maintenance, children’s play provision, public-realm improvements and a fountain within the lake, under an approximately 9.4 million dirham programme. The announced six-month duration is an expectation, not evidence that the work was handed over on schedule. The project joins recreation with care of an ecological site, so a useful outcome account would examine both usable public space and the condition of the lake. A construction announcement alone does not show that either remained satisfactory after opening.

sections.heading: Editorial test for connected everyday access
sections.text: Choose a small set of complete journeys, such as reaching the coach terminal or a local park from different districts. Examine walking access, connecting services, information and the availability of the destination itself. Keep the assessment within the commune while recording dependencies on external transport networks. Parking provisions need observations of the relevant managed areas, and public-space works need completion and maintenance records. Report the same locations and periods when making comparisons. This would make Tangier’s national connections intelligible alongside local service obligations without assuming that major investment automatically improves every resident’s daily journey or neighbourhood environment.

next_artifacts: Dated terminal-access and connecting-service observations with comparable journey definitions.
Implementation and accessibility records for the managed parking areas, without generalizing to all city spaces.
Rahrah completion, maintenance and ecological-condition records, separate from the 2023 forecast.

records.title: Casablanca: transport growth, service contracts and climate planning
records.answer: Casablanca’s local system combines an expanding tram network with delegated municipal services and a developing climate strategy. Its useful evidence includes acknowledged service shortfalls as well as new infrastructure and plans.
records.scope: Commune de Casablanca, counted as one place with sixteen arrondissements. Excludes the wider Casablanca-Settat region and metropolitan transport or utility catchments. Arrondissements, companies and individual transport lines are not additional place identities.
records.stage: Dated council, operating-transport, service-transition and climate-preparation accounts inspected. Planned results and equipment do not establish completed implementation or a city-wide outcome.

identity_decision.rationale: The council's allocation account explicitly identifies sixteen arrondissements within the commune. This profile retains that one municipal identity while describing service providers and networks with potentially wider reach. The Casablanca-Settat region and individual districts are not added as places; no historical acquisition docket is reused.

timeline.event: Council account records an allocation to the commune's sixteen arrondissements.
Casa Transport announces integrated tests for T3 and T4.
Operator confirms T3/T4 are in service; publication is not assigned as their exact opening day.
Climate-plan preparation launched, according to the later municipal article.
Municipality acknowledges uneven service during the cleanliness-contract transition.
Municipality publishes climate-planning progress and a prospective September results window.

sections.heading: One commune with sixteen arrondissements
sections.text: The council’s November 3, 2021 allocation account identifies sixteen arrondissements within the Commune de Casablanca. They are administrative parts of one counted city, not sixteen separate place dossiers. The allocation decision is also a distinct financial stage: it does not show what was subsequently spent or how services performed. Keeping that boundary visible matters when wider metropolitan transport figures or Casablanca-Settat regional programmes enter the discussion. They may describe important dependencies without supplying a municipal denominator. This profile therefore follows the commune and names broader service connections where relevant, rather than treating every nearby investment as a city-level result.

sections.heading: Delivery is distributed across specialist companies
sections.text: The municipal explanation of local development companies describes different delivery roles. Casa Transport develops dedicated public-transport lines, Casa Aménagement handles urban-project functions, and Casa Baïa oversees areas including cleanliness contractors, green spaces and environmental services. These are institutional responsibilities, not interchangeable measures of municipal performance. A problem encountered on a journey may involve several of them: street works, a transport stop and the condition of surrounding public space. The role description helps direct the next question to the appropriate body. It does not show that a contract achieved its standards or that every responsibility has the same geographic reach.

sections.heading: Tram testing and operating introduction are separate
sections.text: Casa Transport’s February 19, 2024 announcement describes integrated tests for T3 and T4, including compatibility with T1/T2 and recovery after disruption. RATP Dev’s October 10 account subsequently confirms that the two new lines are in service and describes connections with the established tram and busway network. The two records show different stages, rather than a test announcement standing in for an operating result. The operator’s estimate of more than twenty million journeys in 2025 remains a forecast. Neither that estimate nor the launch service pattern provides a present-day timetable or a measured account of reliable transfers across modes.

sections.heading: Cleanliness contracts reveal an implementation gap
sections.text: The July 4, 2026 municipal notice acknowledges uneven service in some areas during the transition to new delegated cleanliness contracts. It says those conditions fall short of expectations and contract requirements, while describing daily follow-up and equipment still to be deployed. That is a substantive implementation issue, not merely an announcement of a new procurement arrangement. The notice also distinguishes household collection from arrangements for large waste producers. A later assessment should follow the affected areas, service standards and actual equipment deployment. The commitment to improve does not establish that the shortfalls were resolved by the inspection date.

sections.heading: Climate planning starts with a diagnostic stage
sections.text: The July 20, 2026 account reports that preparation of the Casablanca Climate Plan was launched on July 3 with World Bank support, within the municipal action plan for 2023–2028. It spans mobility, energy, water, waste, urban development and biodiversity, with data collection and diagnostics underway. Intermediate results were expected at the end of September before an operational roadmap. This is preparation, not adoption of a finished climate strategy. The expected results date is neither a retrieved deliverable nor proof that nothing was published. Subsequent evidence needs to show the actual priorities, responsibilities, budgets and measures selected.

sections.heading: Editorial test for improvements that residents can use
sections.text: Connect the systems through specific neighbourhoods and repeatable service questions. A new tram connection can be assessed alongside the cleanliness and accessibility of its approach, while climate priorities can identify which local risks the investment is intended to address. Preserve the provider, geography and reporting period for each measure. Keep complaints, completed interventions and sustained service quality separate. This would allow an acknowledged shortfall to be followed through correction instead of disappearing behind a later investment announcement. The aim is a readable account of changing conditions, with responsibility and delivery stages visible, rather than an unsupported overall score for Casablanca.

next_artifacts: Comparable tram service, interchange and access results, separate from forecasts and launch schedules.
Dated resolution and performance evidence for the cleanliness-contract transition by service area.
Published climate diagnostics and adopted priorities with budgets and responsibilities, distinct from the preparation announcement.
